section: AVI-SPL meeting room reference designs: room types, UC platforms, sustainability-screened designs and ADA considerations
body:
AVI-SPL publishes reference designs and best practices for meeting rooms, curated and configured from its decades of meeting room experience and client work. They give a customer a standard starting point when planning rooms across an organization.

**What to know**

- The room designs aim to give all hybrid participants an equitable, accessible and positive experience.
- Supported UC platforms named: Microsoft Teams, Cisco Webex, Zoom and Google Meet.
- Room designs listed:
  - Mobile Collaboration Space
  - Small Meeting Room
  - Medium Meeting Room
  - Large Conference Room
  - Classroom and Training Room

**Why standardize (end-user and IT benefits)**

- Because the designs follow collaboration technology standards, both end users and IT support staff save time.
- With the same tools and applications in every conference room, teams know how to use each space.
- Help desk teams have fewer solutions to support.
- Other benefits named: higher productivity, better employee experience and satisfaction, and higher video adoption rates.

**Sustainability-screened designs**

- These are described as global meeting room technology standards designed to reduce carbon footprint.
- AVI-SPL has partnered with Logitech to develop sustainability-screened meeting room designs that minimize environmental footprint. The page says they are available now and can be deployed globally.
- More eco-friendly reference designs with other partners are marked as coming soon.

**Real-Time Design**

- With its Real-Time Design approach, AVI-SPL uses 3D visualizations so a customer can validate designs and technology integrations before investing in and building them.

**Accessibility and ADA standards**

The page says designs for outfitting meeting rooms, integrating AV and deploying UC applications should follow the latest ADA Standards, and that AVI-SPL's design and engineering teams can help. Top considerations listed:

- Placement of furniture, and clearance
- Room controls that everyone can reach
- Touch-less interfaces, for example mobile apps and voice control
- Options for people on the team with hearing and vision challenges
- Making sure remote attendees are seen and heard clearly by everyone in the room, and that on-site employees can see and hear virtual attendees

**When to use this**

For customers asking whether AVI-SPL has standard room designs, which room sizes and platforms they cover, how standards help IT, and what accessibility points to plan for.

**Not stated in this source**: equipment lists, capacities or dimensions for each room type, and prices.
